title: Recursive Self-Aggregation Unlocks Deep Thinking in Large Language Models

mechanism.domainTask: Test-time scaling for mathematical, coding, general, and knowledge reasoning
mechanism.populationDetail: Maintains a flat population of N reasoning trajectories for one query; each generation is formed by aggregating uniformly sampled subsets of the current population.
mechanism.archiveDetail: No persistent best-so-far or elite archive is maintained; the final answer is sampled uniformly from the last population in the experiments.
mechanism.replacementDetail: The full population \(P_t\) is replaced by N newly aggregated candidates \(P_{t+1}\); there is no survivor selection or genealogy retention.
mechanism.generationDetail: For the principal K>1 setting, one child reasoning chain is generated by aggregating useful reasoning from K true parent candidates sampled from the current population.
mechanism.feedbackDetail: RSA has no explicit per-candidate score or verifier in its inference loop; the LLM is prompted to implicitly assess and improve the supplied reasoning chains. Benchmark answer correctness is for reporting, not in-loop feedback.
mechanism.parentSelectionDetail: K is configurable; the main comparison uses K=4, while other settings vary K. N aggregation subsets are sampled from the same current population at each step.
mechanism.outOfTaxonomy: Inference-time population reasoning uses implicit self-verification through recursive aggregation without an explicit objective evaluator; aggregation-aware RL additionally adapts model weights to this inference-time procedure.
